most tumors from p53-deficient mice have a normal mutation frequency, and that most mutations are point mutations, with deletions, insertations and indels occurring at a much lower frequency.

most tumors in the p53+/+ and p53+/- murines have a normal mutation frequency with a normal mutation pattern, that the majority of tumors in p53-/- mice show normal mutation frequency, but a minority have a low mutation frequency, and that alterations in mutation pattern are uncommon, tumor specific, and not necessarily associated increases in mutation frequency.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tumors from the p53+/- mouse model do not have a high frequency of mutations or a mutator phenotype, but that the data do not exclude a low frequency of mutations in some tumors.
most tumors in the p53+/- mouse model of Li Fraumeni syndrome do have a normal mutation frequency, and a normal mutation signature.
tumors from the p53+/- murines have normal mutation load, and the data are consistent with a lack of a mutator phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tumors from p53-deficient animals do not have a high mutation frequency or a mutator phenotype.
most spontaneous tumors in p53+/– mice have normal mutation frequency and pattern.
most tumors in the p53+/- mouse have a normal mutation load and pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vast majority of spontaneous tumors in p53+/- and p53-/- mice have a normal mutation frequency, which is not the case in tumors from mismatch repair-deficient mice.
most p53+/- tumors do not have a high mutation load, and that the mutation load in a tumor does not necessarily correlate with the mutation pattern.
the vast majority of p53+/- tumors have a normal mutation load and pattern.
